headline: A counterfeiter hand-painted $50 bills for 18 years — a wet bar counter ended it

sources.title: Kings of Counterfeiting — American Numismatic Society

summary: German-born Emanuel Ninger, nicknamed "Jim the Penman," hand-painted counterfeit US notes from about 1878: soaking bond paper in weak coffee, tracing real notes over glass, and painting silk threads in red and blue ink. In March 1896 a $50 note got wet on the counter of a Manhattan tavern; the ink smudged and the forgery was exposed. He was sentenced in May 1896 to six years. He had confessed to about 390 notes, with estimates up to roughly 700. He died in 1924 in Pennsylvania. His exact birth year (c. 1846) is disputed and should not be stated precisely.
